## Conclusions
- **tanh GELU saves nothing on the S22:** 14.43 vs 14.41 ms image, 3.26 vs 3.26 ms text. The QNN converter fuses
  both the erf and the tanh pattern into the same `Gelu` op (`node_Gelu_37`: 1.64M vs 1.63M cycles in block 3), so
  the swap is a no-op after compilation.
- **Sigmoid GELU (QuickGELU) is 12% faster end to end:** image 14.41 -> 12.64 ms (-1.77, -12%), text 3.26 -> 2.84 ms
  (-0.42, -13%), **total 17.67 -> 15.48 ms (-2.19 ms, -12.4%)**. It is not fused: Sigmoid + Mul run at 1.04M cycles
  per block vs 1.63M for the fused `Gelu`. Summed image cycles drop 58.6M -> 50.7M (-13%), which here does track
  wall time.
- **Accuracy without retraining (024):** QuickGELU costs -0.75 [-1.4, -0.1] on RefCOCOg-LPCVC and -1.15 [-1.9, -0.4]
  on grouped; the sample is +0.27 (noise; device sample R@10 91.64 vs 91.37).
- Profiles are stable (3 runs, spread <= 0.26 ms) and the control reproduces 011 (17.67 vs 17.68 ms). Peak memory
  and ONNX size are unchanged.
- **Decision / next:** tanh GELU is dropped. QuickGELU is a real NPU-aware architecture change (the GELU is the
  largest FP16 op cost). It is worth one fine-tune with QuickGELU in place (010 recipe, ~22 min), to see whether
  the ~1-point loss disappears while keeping the -2.2 ms. Not run yet.
